title: Court Register distribution command
description: Body of a message on the ASB queue yotresultsdistribution.requests. This is the inbound queue message contract, agreed jointly with cpp-context-results (results-event-processor), which publishes one message per resulted hearing. The message is a claim check: the hearing payload is fetched separately from Redis, with the results query API as fallback. Any change to this schema is a cross-team change and must be agreed with the Results team first. The narrative companion is the Confluence design page; if the two disagree, this schema plus its tests win.

source.description: Publishing system. Half of the idempotency key: it namespaces requestId so a future second publisher cannot collide with Results.

requestId.description: Publisher-minted, deterministic from hearingId, hearingDay and sharedTime. A republish of the same share carries the same id; a genuine re-share produces a new sharedTime and so a new id, and must be reprocessed.

hearingId.description: The resulted hearing. One court register is produced per hearing, so this is also the unit of output. With hearingDay it forms the Redis cache key and the query-API fallback path.

hearingDay.description: The hearing day this share relates to, as YYYY-MM-DD. The pattern is RFC 3339 full-date, stated here rather than left to whichever validator reads `format`: `date` is checked by a different implementation in every consumer, and this contract's grammar is a four-digit unsigned year, a two-digit month and a two-digit day, with no expanded or signed year form. The `format` keyword still does the semantic half — 30 February and 29 February in a common year are refused by it, not by the pattern. It keys the Redis claim-check (INT_{hearingId}_{hearingDay}_result_) and NOTHING else. It is deliberately not called hearingDate: the legacy trigger renames it that way (CourtRegisterEventGridTrigger/index.js:15, CourtRegisterQueueTrigger/index.js:16), which collides with the register's own hearing date - derived from the latest judicialResult.orderedDate - and with the register date derived from sharedTime. The three dates are distinct and must never be conflated (design doc 2.2).

sharedTime.description: ISO-8601 instant at which the hearing was shared. The pattern is the contract's grammar, narrower than draft-07's `date-time` format on three points, each of which this service's parser already refused: (1) the separator is T or t only — RFC 3339's ABNF is date-time = full-date "T" full-time, and the space form appears only in the readability note of section 5.6, which merely permits an application to accept it; (2) the seconds field never reaches 60 — a leap second is grammatical in RFC 3339 but unrepresentable in java.time, so accepting one would mean inventing a value to store, and deciding which :60 instants were real needs a leap-second table nobody wants on a contract's hot path; (3) -00:00 is excluded, because RFC 3339 gives it the distinct meaning `offset unknown` and this field is a true instant. The lower-case t and z forms are permitted, and so is an offset of +00:00. `format` still does the semantic half: an impossible date or hour is refused by it, not by the pattern. Narrowed 2026-08-31 (the Confluence design page) so the schema and the parser agree on every form with no exemption list; no producer is live yet, and nothing cpp-context-results can emit reaches any excluded form, because it serialises with Instant.toString(). It is the true instant, never re-labelled through a timezone conversion (fix C10), and it yields the register date that drives the reference-data on= day (fix C12), the progression batching key and the register filename (fix C11).

eventType.description: Hearing_Resulted only, and there is no second value pending: unlike the informant flow, the court register has no SJP leg at all. Any other value is a non-transient failure (dead-letter with reason), never a silent skip.

userId.description: OPTIONAL. The CPP user who shared the hearing results, carried so that every downstream call made for this message is attributed to that user through CJSCPPUID - which is what the function app does today: the hearing-resulted envelope's userId becomes the orchestration's cjscppuid (CourtRegisterEventGridTrigger/index.js:16, CourtRegisterQueueTrigger/index.js:17) and is threaded unchanged into the payload read, the now-subscriptions read (NowsHelper/service/ReferenceDataService.js:44) and the add-court-register POST (ProcessOutboundCourtRegister/index.js:19). Optional rather than required because two legitimate producers of this message have no user to name: support replay tooling, where the replay is built by hand rather than re-sent verbatim, or is re-sent deliberately without the field because the original user has been deactivated - a replay that IS re-sent verbatim still names the user the original named, and is attributed to them; and any producer build from before this field existed - the transition window. The consumer must therefore accept a message both ways, and a message carrying no userId is processed under the service's own configured system identity. A userId that IS present must be a canonical UUID; anything else is a schema violation and dead-letters like any other, because a value that cannot be an identity must not be sent as one.
